items.note: Plate caption names the Pisanhārī kā Mandir at Udayapur, Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh.
Plate caption records a view of the mihrab of the mosque on the western side (of the Udayeśvara temple).
Temple built in the second half of the 11th century CE by Udayāditya Paramāra, who ascended the throne in 1070 CE.
Udayāditya patronised art and architecture, founded the city of Udayapur in modern Vidisha and built several temples, the most famous being the Udayeśvara.
Quotes the Udayapur Praśasti on Udayāditya as 'another sun' destroying his foes, highlighting his military might.
Temple is Bhūmija; Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra is among the earliest śilpaśāstras referring to the style, which the Paramāras seem to have developed to maturity.

claim.value: earlier antecedents; Paramāras of Malwa developed it to maturity

items.note: Discusses Bhūmija as 'born from the earth': native style of Malwa, also found in Rajasthan and northern Maharashtra, or terrestrial rather than divine origin.
Another sense of Bhūmija: kūṭas arranged vertically give the appearance of rising from the ground.
Distinctive Bhūmija feature: śikhara with four latās and rows of miniature śikharas (kūṭastambhas) between them.
Śūrsenaka medallions on north, south and west; east latā ends in śukanāsa; temples are nirandhāra.
Red sandstone, east-facing temple with garbhagṛha, antarāla, gūḍhamaṇḍapa, three mukhamaṇḍapas and a separate vedī; on a lofty jagatī with eight subsidiary shrines.
Original entrance by stairway flanked by Śaiva pratihāras, now from the west; sanctum stellate-cum-circular, saptaratha, saptabhūmi.
Bhūmija plan: the square rotates about its centre (parivartanā) rather than being divided as a grid.
Pīṭha has five mouldings: bhiṭṭa 1 and 2, jādyakumbha, karṇaka and grāsapaṭṭī; ornament of bhiṭṭa 2.
Describes jādyakumbha, karṇaka and the grāsapaṭṭī band of kīrtimukha heads.
Vedibandha mouldings: khura with ratnapaṭṭī, karṇikā, kumbha with khattikā niches and manibandha, kalaśa with gagārapaṭṭī.
Buttresses appear to rise from the ground (Bhūmija), pillar-like in the jaṅghā and continuing as kūṭastambhas in the śikhara.
Kūṭastambhas one below another resemble pearl strings suspended from the śikhara, interrupted by the flat latās with gavākṣa lace work.
Gūḍhamaṇḍapa has a samvarṇā bell-roof and three projecting mukhamaṇḍapas; main entrance from the east by steps.
The śikhara is distinctive of the Bhūmija, with four flat latās decorated with gavākṣa lace-work.
Seven bhūmis of kūṭastambhas per sub-quarter, decreasing in size toward the skandha whose edges articulate the star-shaped plan.
Unusual figure on the north-west śikhara, possibly a flag bearer hoisting the flag of victory.
Śukanāsa caitya has a lower pillared shrine with two dancing goddesses and an upper caitya gavākṣa with dancing Śiva and goddesses.
Makara-rider design component compared with the Draupadi Ratha, Durga Temple at Aihole and Ellora; possibly travelled to Southeast Asia.
Earliest textual reference to figures atop makaras is the Viṣṇudharmottara Mahāpurāṇa.
Amaravati and Ajanta figures on crocodiles may have been prototypes for the figures at Udayeśvara.
Multi-armed Naṭeśa Śiva in the upper medallion of the śukanāsa performs the tāṇḍava in ūrdhvajānu karaṇa, with dancing devīs and gaṇas.
Lotus-bud necklace of the śukanāsa Sarasvatī; Bhoja as patron of learning and arts, so Sarasvatī often depicted in Paramāra sculpture and invoked in Paramāra epigraphs.
Udayeśvara Sarasvatī shows fine workmanship and is unusually depicted as a dancer; dancing Sarasvatī images are rare.
Nāṭyaśāstra describes Śiva as progenitor of the tāṇḍava and Pārvatī performing the graceful aspect.
The dance of Śiva and Pārvatī seems to have been sculpted in the śukanāsa at Udayeśvara.
Abhinavagupta on drums and viṇā accompanying the tāṇḍava explains Sarasvatī's presence; the artist shows her dancing instead.
Hariharārkapitāmaha image in the śukanāsa niche: three visible faces, eight hands, Sūrya central.
Aparājitapṛcchā of Gujarat prescribes the Hariharahiranyagarbha image: four gods amalgamated, four faces, eight hands.
Composite Hariharahiranyagarbha images follow Śilpaśāstra injunctions; central deity is Sūrya or Viṣṇu, found in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Central India.
Śukanāsa composition related to the śuddha addhvā of Śaiva Siddhānta: Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara and Sadvidyā.
Five-storeyed celestial mansion on each side of the śukanāsa with five Śiva and five devī images in all.
Attributes of Māheśvarī, Sarvamaṅgalā and Śiva in the northern celestial mansion.
Śriyā image with iguana vāhana, holding a preta; possibly symbolising the enemy to be destroyed.
Three śūrasenakas resemble the śukanāsa but smaller; all contain Śiva Naṭeśa.
Miniature shrine below the west śūrasenaka houses a seated six-armed Śiva of fine workmanship.
Image possibly Mṛtyuñjaya with snake ornaments; since the temple was built for victory, Śiva-Mṛtyuñjaya would help overcome death on the battlefield.
Śaiva pratihāras, vyāla and gaja decoration and miniature four-armed Śiva shrines at the west śūrasenaka.
South śūrasenaka has Śiva dancing in ūrdhvajānu with similar weapons; seated Śiva below.
North śūrasenaka Śiva has a gajahasta of the tāṇḍava, differing attributes.
Maṇḍovara buttresses resemble faceted pillars with khattaka niches; salilāntara carved with lotus scrolls and apsarās; same pattern on garbhagṛha and gūḍhamaṇḍapa.
Two sets of niches: khattikās on the kumbha with Umā-Maheśvara, dikpālas, Gaṇeśa; larger khattakas on the jaṅghā.
Standing multi-armed Mahābhairava with skull garland, snake-hood head-dress and dog.
Bhairava iconography text; since the Paramāras were strong patrons of Śaivism, several Bhairava images found in Malwa.
Sūrya in a khattaka flanked by attendants Daṇḍī and Piṅgala.
Dikpālas are on khattakas of the central or second buttress of the gūḍhamaṇḍapa; Indra on the east.
Indra in abhaṅga with vajra and elephant vāhana; Kāmikāgama description cited.
Book in Agni's hand read as symbolising Vedic sacrifices and scriptures, linked to Śaiva Siddhānta caryā fire rituals.
Ardhanārīśvara on the east face of the third buttress: Śiva right half, Pārvatī left half with mounts.
Four-armed Harihara with Śiva and Viṣṇu halves and vāhanas Nandi and Garuḍa.
Devatāmūrtiprakaraṇa prescription for Harihara; the image conforms closely to the description.
Multi-armed Śiva Naṭeśa near the south mukhamaṇḍapa, an ūrdhvatāṇḍava image.
